records.source: הַדָּבָ֛ר אֲשֶׁר־הָיָ֥ה אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וּנְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֣ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֣ל׀וְכָל־חֵיל֡וֹ וְכָל־מַמְלְכ֣וֹת אֶרֶץ֩ מֶמְשֶׁ֨לֶת יָד֜וֹ וְכָל־הָעַמִּ֗ים נִלְחָמִ֧ים עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֛ם וְעַל־כָּל־עָרֶ֖יהָ לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: The word which came to Jeremiah from with Yahweh, while Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon and all his army and all [the] kingdoms of [the] earth of [the] dominion of his hand and all the peoples [were] fighting against Jerusalem and against all its cities, saying:
pieces: This message came to Jeremiah from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} while Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon was making war on Jerusalem and all its towns, with his whole army and all the kingdoms and peoples of the earth that were under his rule:

L.1: The word that came to Jeremiah from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon and all his army, and all the kingdoms of the earth under the dominion of his hand, and all the peoples were fighting against Jerusalem and against all its cities, saying:

R.1: This is the message {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Jeremiah. It came while Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon was attacking Jerusalem and all the towns around it. His whole army was with him, and so were soldiers from all the kingdoms and peoples he ruled.

decisions.choice: the setting: the Babylonian siege of Jerusalem in Zedekiah's last years (588-587 BC)
decisions.reason: Zedekiah rebelled against Babylon, and Nebuchadrezzar came with his army and laid siege to Jerusalem in Zedekiah's ninth year (39:1; 52:4; 2 Kings 25:1). Verse 7 shows that the siege was still early: two other fortified towns of Judah were still holding out.

decisions.choice: the kingdoms of the earth under the dominion of his hand: the subject nations that sent troops with him
decisions.reason: Babylon ruled a wide empire, and the peoples under its rule had to supply soldiers for its wars. The phrase stresses the size of the force that has come against Jerusalem. "The earth" here means the lands of Babylon's empire, as in 27:6-7.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar: the same king as Nebuchadnezzar
decisions.reason: This chapter uses the spelling with r, as Jeremiah usually does (21:2). It is one man either way.

decisions.choice: the heading introduces the word of verses 2-5
decisions.reason: "Saying" leads into the word itself, which begins with the LORD's command to Jeremiah in verse 2.

decisions.choice: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD (L); This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD (B); This is the message the LORD gave Jeremiah (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this heading throughout Jeremiah. Balanced moves the list of attackers after the verb so the sentence reads clearly; Readable breaks it into three sentences.

decisions.choice: towns
decisions.reason: The "cities" of Judah were mostly small walled towns, so Balanced and Readable say "towns", as elsewhere in Jeremiah. Literal keeps "cities".

records.heading: A message for King Zedekiah

records.source: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הָלֹךְ֙ וְאָ֣מַרְתָּ֔ אֶל־צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֗יו כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִ֨י נֹתֵ֜ן אֶת־הָעִ֤יר הַזֹּאת֙ בְּיַ֣ד מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֔ל וּשְׂרָפָ֖הּ בָּאֵֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh, [the] God of Israel: Go, and you will say to Zedekiah king of Judah, and you will say to him: Thus says Yahweh: Look I [am] giving the city this into [the] hand of [the] king of Babylon, and he will burn it with the fire.
pieces: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says this: Go to Zedekiah king of Judah and tell him, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: I am about to hand this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will burn it down.

L.2: "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel: Go and speak to Zedekiah king of Judah, and say to him, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Look, I am giving this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will burn it with fire.

R.2: "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says: Go to Zedekiah king of Judah and give him this message: 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I am going to hand this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will burn it to the ground.

decisions.choice: two speeches, one inside the other
decisions.reason: The LORD first speaks to Jeremiah ("Go and say"), and then gives him the words to carry to the king, which run to the end of verse 5.

decisions.choice: giving into the hand of: handing over to the power of
decisions.reason: To give something into someone's hand is to put it under that person's control. The same words were spoken to Zedekiah in 21:10 and are repeated in 32:3 and 37:8.

decisions.choice: the burning of the city
decisions.reason: The Babylonians burned the temple, the palace and the houses of Jerusalem when the city fell in 586 BC (39:8; 52:13).

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD (L); The LORD says this (B); This is what the LORD says (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula in Isaiah and Jeremiah. Balanced and Readable leave out "look" and give its force as "about to" and "going to".

records.source: וְאַתָּ֗ה לֹ֚א תִמָּלֵט֙ מִיָּד֔וֹ כִּ֚י תָּפֹ֣שׂ תִּתָּפֵ֔שׂ וּבְיָד֖וֹ תִּנָּתֵ֑ן וְֽ֠עֵינֶיךָ אֶת־עֵינֵ֨י מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֜ל תִּרְאֶ֗ינָה וּפִ֛יהוּ אֶת־פִּ֥יךָ יְדַבֵּ֖ר וּבָבֶ֥ל תָּבֽוֹא׃
records.gloss: And you, not you will escape from his hand, for surely you will be captured, and into his hand you will be given; and your eyes the eyes of [the] king of Babylon will see, and his mouth with your mouth will speak, and Babylon you will go.
pieces: You yourself will not escape from him. You will certainly be captured and handed over to him. You will look the king of Babylon in the eye, and he will speak to you face to face. And you will go to Babylon.

L.3: And you will not escape from his hand, for you will surely be captured and given into his hand; and your eyes will see the eyes of the king of Babylon, and his mouth will speak with your mouth, and you will go [to] Babylon.

R.3: You will not get away from him. You will be caught and handed over to him. You will stand in front of the king of Babylon and see him with your own eyes, and he will speak to you in person. Then you will be taken to Babylon.

decisions.choice: eyes seeing eyes, mouth speaking with mouth: meeting in person
decisions.reason: The two pictures say that Zedekiah will be brought before the king of Babylon himself and will face him. The same words are said to him in 32:4. It happened at Riblah, where Nebuchadrezzar passed sentence on him (39:5-7; 52:9-11; 2 Kings 25:6-7).

decisions.choice: surely captured: the verb doubled for certainty
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the verb, "capturing you will be captured", which makes the statement emphatic: there is no doubt about it.

decisions.choice: and you: the king set beside the city
decisions.reason: Verse 2 spoke of the city; the separate pronoun "you" turns to Zedekiah himself. The city will burn, and the king will not get away either.

decisions.choice: look the king of Babylon in the eye ... face to face (B); see him with your own eyes ... in person (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say in common English what the two Hebrew pictures mean (m1). Literal keeps them as they are.

decisions.choice: you will be taken to Babylon
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "you will go". Readable makes clear that he goes as a prisoner, as 39:7 and 52:11 tell.

records.source: אַ֚ךְ שְׁמַ֣ע דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ עָלֶ֔יךָ לֹ֥א תָמ֖וּת בֶּחָֽרֶב׃
records.gloss: Only hear [the] word of Yahweh, Zedekiah king of Judah: Thus says Yahweh concerning you: Not you will die by the sword.
pieces: But hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, Zedekiah king of Judah. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this about you: You will not die by the sword.

L.4: Yet hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, Zedekiah king of Judah: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} concerning you: You will not die by the sword.

R.4: But listen to what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says, Zedekiah king of Judah. This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says about you: You will not be killed in battle.

decisions.choice: yet: a word of comfort set against the warning
decisions.reason: The small word turns the message. After the loss of the city and his own capture (verses 2-3), the king is told something he can hold on to.

decisions.choice: die by the sword: be killed violently
decisions.reason: The sword stands for violent death, in battle or at the hand of the enemy. Zedekiah's sons and the nobles of Judah were killed in this way (39:6), but the king himself was not.

decisions.choice: The LORD says this about you (B); This is what the LORD says about you (R)
decisions.reason: The book's wording for "Thus says the LORD" at each level, with "about you" for "concerning you".

decisions.choice: killed in battle
decisions.reason: Readable says what dying "by the sword" means here (m2).

records.source: בְּשָׁל֣וֹם תָּמ֗וּת וּֽכְמִשְׂרְפ֣וֹת אֲ֠בוֹתֶיךָ הַמְּלָכִ֨ים הָרִֽאשֹׁנִ֜ים אֲשֶׁר־הָי֣וּ לְפָנֶ֗יךָ כֵּ֚ן יִשְׂרְפוּ־לָ֔ךְ וְה֥וֹי אָד֖וֹן יִסְפְּדוּ־לָ֑ךְ כִּֽי־דָבָ֥ר אֲנִֽי־דִבַּ֖רְתִּי נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: In peace you will die; and as [the] burnings of your fathers, the kings the former who were before you, so they will burn for you, and Alas, lord! they will lament for you; for [a] word I have spoken, declaration of Yahweh.
pieces: You will die in peace. As spices were burned in honor of your ancestors, the kings who ruled before you, so people will burn spices in your honor and mourn for you, crying, 'Alas, my lord!' I have given {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'"

L.5: In peace you will die; and as with the burnings for your fathers, the former kings who were before you, so they will burn [spices] for you, and they will lament for you, 'Alas, lord!' For I have spoken the word, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'"

R.5: You will die in peace. When your ancestors, the kings before you, died, people burned spices to honor them. They will do the same for you. They will weep for you and cry out, 'How sad, our master!' I have promised it, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'"

decisions.choice: the burnings: fragrant spices burned at a king's funeral
decisions.reason: At the burial of a king of Judah his people burned spices and perfumes in great quantity to honor him: Asa was laid on a bed full of spices and "they made a very great burning for him" (2 Chronicles 16:14), and the people made no such burning for the wicked Jehoram (2 Chronicles 21:19). The body itself was not burned; Israel buried its dead. Zedekiah is promised the honors of a king at his death.

decisions.choice: Alas, lord!: the cry of mourning for a dead king
decisions.reason: The cry here is the wail of a funeral, not a threat of judgment. The same cry is denied to King Jehoiakim in 22:18: "They will not lament for him, 'Alas, my brother!' ... 'Alas, lord!'" Zedekiah, unlike his brother, will be mourned.

decisions.choice: die in peace: a natural death, not by the sword, with mourning and burial
alternatives: a promise that depended on Zedekiah obeying the word and surrendering
decisions.reason: "In peace" is set against "by the sword" in verse 4: he will not be killed. The promise must be read with what happened. Zedekiah saw his sons killed, was blinded and was taken to Babylon in chains, where he stayed in prison until he died (39:6-7; 52:10-11; 2 Kings 25:7). Yet he did die a natural death, and the honors of verse 5 may have been given him among the exiles. Some read the promise as depending on his surrender, which Jeremiah later urged on him as the way to save his life and the city (38:17-18); the text here does not state a condition.

decisions.choice: for I have spoken the word: the LORD stands behind the promise
decisions.reason: The emphatic "I" stresses who has said it: the word is the LORD's own pledge, so the king may trust it.

decisions.choice: spices (L in brackets; B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "they will burn for you". All three levels name what was burned (m1), Literal in brackets.

decisions.choice: Alas, my lord (B); How sad, our master (R)
decisions.reason: The cry is "Alas, lord!". Balanced adds "my", as English mourners would say it, and Readable says "our master". "Alas" (Literal, Balanced) and "How sad" (Readable) are the wording for this funeral cry, as in 22:18.

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּר֙ יִרְמְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֔יא אֶל־צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה אֵ֛ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: And spoke Jeremiah the prophet to Zedekiah king of Judah all the words these in Jerusalem,
pieces: Jeremiah the prophet told Zedekiah king of Judah all these things in Jerusalem,

L.6: And Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Zedekiah king of Judah all these words in Jerusalem,

R.6: Jeremiah the prophet gave this whole message to Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: one sentence with verse 7
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence runs on into verse 7, which says when Jeremiah spoke: while the Babylonian army was still fighting against Jerusalem, Lachish and Azekah.

decisions.choice: in Jerusalem: inside the besieged city
decisions.reason: Jeremiah was free to go in and out at this point (37:4); later he was shut up in the guard courtyard of the palace (32:2; 37:21).

decisions.choice: two sentences
decisions.reason: Readable ends the sentence here and starts a new one with verse 7.

records.source: וְחֵ֣יל מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֗ל נִלְחָמִים֙ עַל־יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְעַ֛ל כָּל־עָרֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה הַנּֽוֹתָר֑וֹת אֶל־לָכִישׁ֙ וְאֶל־עֲזֵקָ֔ה כִּ֣י הֵ֗נָּה נִשְׁאֲר֛וּ בְּעָרֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה עָרֵ֥י מִבְצָֽר׃פ
records.gloss: while [the] army of [the] king of Babylon [was] fighting against Jerusalem and against all [the] cities of Judah, the [ones] left, against Lachish and against Azekah; for they remained among [the] cities of Judah [as] cities of fortification.
pieces: while the king of Babylon's army was attacking Jerusalem and the towns of Judah that were still holding out, Lachish and Azekah. These were the only fortified towns of Judah that remained.

L.7: while the army of the king of Babylon was fighting against Jerusalem and against all the cities of Judah that were left, against Lachish and against Azekah; for these remained among the cities of Judah as fortified cities.

R.7: At that time the army of the king of Babylon was attacking Jerusalem and the other towns of Judah that had not yet been captured. These were Lachish and Azekah, the only towns with strong walls that were still left in Judah.

decisions.choice: Lachish and Azekah: fortress towns in the low hills southwest of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Lachish was the strongest city of Judah after Jerusalem, and Azekah lay to its north, guarding the valley of Elah (1 Samuel 17:1). Rehoboam had fortified both (2 Chronicles 11:9). Letters written on pieces of pottery, found in the ruins of the gate of Lachish and dating from these years, include one in which an officer says he can no longer see the signals of Azekah, a vivid glimpse of the towns falling one by one.

decisions.choice: the cities that were left: the few towns not yet taken
decisions.reason: The Babylonians had taken the rest of Judah. Only these two fortified towns and Jerusalem itself were still standing when Jeremiah spoke.

decisions.choice: still holding out ... the only fortified towns (B); had not yet been captured ... towns with strong walls (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "left" and "cities of fortification" mean in a war: towns that had not yet fallen, protected by strong walls.

records.source: הַדָּבָ֛ר אֲשֶׁר־הָיָ֥ה אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה אַחֲרֵ֡י כְּרֹת֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֜הוּ בְּרִ֗ית אֶת־כָּל־הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּירֽוּשָׁלִַ֔ם לִקְרֹ֥א לָהֶ֖ם דְּרֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: The word which came to Jeremiah from with Yahweh after made the king Zedekiah [a] covenant with all the people who [were] in Jerusalem to proclaim to them liberty,
pieces: This message came to Jeremiah from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} after King Zedekiah and all the people in Jerusalem had made a covenant to announce freedom,

L.8: The word that came to Jeremiah from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, after King Zedekiah had made a covenant with all the people who were in Jerusalem to proclaim liberty to them,

R.8: This is the message {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Jeremiah after King Zedekiah made a covenant with all the people in Jerusalem. They agreed to announce freedom for their slaves.

decisions.choice: the heading is broken off and taken up again in verse 12
decisions.reason: The heading names the word that came to Jeremiah, but before the word is given the narrator tells the story behind it (verses 8-11). Verse 12 starts the heading again, "the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah", and the word itself follows in verses 13-22.

decisions.choice: proclaim liberty: the release of the Jubilee in Leviticus 25:10
decisions.reason: The word means release, especially the freeing of people held for debt. In Leviticus 25:10 Israel is to "proclaim liberty in the land to all its inhabitants" in the fiftieth year. King and people do here what that law describes. The same word returns in verses 15 and 17, and in Isaiah 61:1.

decisions.choice: a covenant made by the king with the people: a solemn agreement sworn in the temple
decisions.reason: The king and the people bound themselves by oath before the LORD (verse 15) with the rite described in verses 18-19. The text does not say what moved them. It was made during the siege (verse 7), perhaps in hope that the LORD would save the city if the law were kept, or to add men to the defense and to stop feeding slaves in a hungry city.

decisions.choice: liberty (L); freedom (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 25:10: Literal keeps the traditional "liberty", Balanced and Readable say "freedom". Balanced says "announce" for "proclaim", as there.

decisions.choice: for their slaves
decisions.reason: "To them" is unclear on its own; Readable says who was to be freed, as verse 9 goes on to tell.

records.heading: Freed slaves taken back

records.source: לְ֠שַׁלַּח אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־עַבְדּ֞וֹ וְאִ֧ישׁ אֶת־שִׁפְחָת֛וֹ הָעִבְרִ֥י וְהָעִבְרִיָּ֖ה חָפְשִׁ֑ים לְבִלְתִּ֧י עֲבָד־בָּ֛ם בִּיהוּדִ֥י אָחִ֖יהוּ אִֽישׁ׃
records.gloss: to send away each his male slave and each his female slave, the Hebrew [man] and the Hebrew [woman], free, so as not to hold them as slaves, a Judean his brother, anyone.
pieces: so that everyone would set free their Hebrew slaves, both men and women, and no one would keep a fellow Judean as a slave.

L.9: that each should send away free his male slave and each his female slave, the Hebrew man and the Hebrew woman, so that no one should hold them as slaves, a Judean [holding] his brother.

R.9: Everyone was to set free their Hebrew slaves, both men and women. No one was to keep another person from Judah as a slave.

decisions.choice: Hebrew slaves: fellow Israelites owned for a time because of debt
decisions.reason: "Hebrew" is a name for an Israelite, as in the law of release (Exodus 21:2; Deuteronomy 15:12). Such people had been sold, or had sold themselves, through poverty or debt. They were owned and had to work, but the law limited their service to six years (verse 14).

decisions.choice: a Judean his brother: a member of Judah enslaving a fellow member
decisions.reason: "Judean" here means a member of the kingdom of Judah. Calling the slave the owner's "brother" makes the point of the law: one member of God's people is not to own another for good (Leviticus 25:39-42).

decisions.choice: free: released from slavery
decisions.reason: The word means a freed person, no longer owned, as in Exodus 21:2 and Deuteronomy 15:12.

decisions.choice: slave, female slave (L); slaves, male and female (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Slave" stays at every level, as the style guide keeps it where people are owned and released: the whole passage is about setting slaves free and forcing them back into slavery, and "servant" would hide the point.

decisions.choice: each (L); everyone ... their (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "a man" here means each owner, man or woman, so every level uses words that need no gender setting.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ֩ כָל־הַשָּׂרִ֨ים וְכָל־הָעָ֜ם אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֣אוּ בַבְּרִ֗ית לְ֠שַׁלַּח אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־עַבְדּ֞וֹ וְאִ֤ישׁ אֶת־שִׁפְחָתוֹ֙ חָפְשִׁ֔ים לְבִלְתִּ֥י עֲבָד־בָּ֖ם ע֑וֹד וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֖וּ וַיְשַׁלֵּֽחוּ׃
records.gloss: And obeyed all the princes and all the people who entered into the covenant to send away each his male slave and each his female slave free, so as not to hold them as slaves again; and they obeyed and sent [them] away.
pieces: All the officials and all the people who had entered into the covenant agreed to set free their male and female slaves and not keep them as slaves any longer. They obeyed and let them go.

L.10: And all the princes and all the people who had entered into the covenant obeyed, that each would send away free his male slave and each his female slave, so as not to hold them as slaves again; they obeyed and sent [them] away.

R.10: All the leaders and all the people who had made this covenant agreed to it. They would set free their slaves, both men and women, and not keep them as slaves anymore. So they obeyed and let them go.

decisions.choice: obeyed ... obeyed: they agreed to the covenant, and then carried it out
decisions.reason: The verb means to hear, and so to heed or obey. Its first use says they accepted the terms; its second, that they did what they had promised. The repetition sets up the turn in verse 11.

decisions.choice: princes: the officials of the royal court
decisions.reason: These are the king's high officers, who are named again in verse 19.

decisions.choice: slave, female slave (L); slaves, male and female (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Slave" stays at every level, as the style guide keeps it where people are owned and released: the whole passage is about setting slaves free and forcing them back into slavery, and "servant" would hide the point.

decisions.choice: princes (L); officials (B); leaders (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this word in the prophets and the histories.

records.source: וַיָּשׁ֨וּבוּ֙ אַחֲרֵי־כֵ֔ן וַיָּשִׁ֗בוּ אֶת־הָֽעֲבָדִים֙ וְאֶת־הַשְּׁפָח֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר שִׁלְּח֖וּ חָפְשִׁ֑ים וַֽיִּכְבְּשׁ֔וּם לַעֲבָדִ֖ים וְלִשְׁפָחֽוֹת׃ס
records.gloss: But they turned back after thus, and they brought back the male slaves and the female slaves whom they had sent away free, and they subjected them as male slaves and as female slaves.
pieces: But afterward they changed their minds. They took back the men and women they had set free and forced them to be their slaves again.

L.11: But afterward they turned back, and they brought back the male slaves and the female slaves whom they had sent away free, and they subjected them [to be] male slaves and female slaves.

R.11: But later they changed their minds. They took back the slaves they had freed and forced them to be slaves again.

decisions.choice: afterward: when the Babylonian army lifted the siege for a time
decisions.reason: Verses 21-22 say that the army of Babylon "has gone up from you", and 37:5-11 tells how it broke off the siege when an Egyptian army came out. With the danger past, the owners took their slaves back. The LORD's answer is that the army will return (verse 22).

decisions.choice: they turned back and brought back: the same Hebrew verb in two forms
decisions.reason: "Turn" and "bring back" share one root. The word plays through the passage: the people "turned" to do right (verse 15), then "turned" again and "brought back" their slaves (verse 16).

decisions.choice: subjected them: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text has one form of this verb and the scribes noted another in the margin to be read aloud. Both mean to bring under force, to subdue.

decisions.choice: slave, female slave (L); slaves, male and female (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Slave" stays at every level, as the style guide keeps it where people are owned and released: the whole passage is about setting slaves free and forcing them back into slavery, and "servant" would hide the point.

decisions.choice: changed their minds
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "turned back" means here: they went back on their promise.

records.source: וַיְהִ֤י דְבַר־יְהוָה֙ אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to Jeremiah from with Yahweh, saying:
pieces: Then the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to Jeremiah:

L.12: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Jeremiah from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying:

R.12: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Jeremiah this message:

decisions.choice: the heading of verse 8 taken up again
decisions.reason: After the story of verses 8-11, the narrator resumes the heading. The double mention of the LORD, "the word of the LORD ... from the LORD", is unusual and stresses where the word comes from.

decisions.choice: the LORD gave Jeremiah this message
decisions.reason: Readable gives the heading in the plain form used for it in Jeremiah and does not repeat the divine name. Balanced keeps both names but puts "from the LORD" before "to Jeremiah".

records.source: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אָנֹכִ֗י כָּרַ֤תִּֽי בְרִית֙ אֶת־אֲב֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם בְּי֨וֹם הוֹצִאִ֤י אוֹתָם֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם מִבֵּ֥ית עֲבָדִ֖ים לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh, [the] God of Israel: I made [a] covenant with your fathers in [the] day of my bringing them out from [the] land of Egypt, from [the] house of slaves, saying:
pieces: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says this: I made a covenant with your ancestors when I led them out of the land of Egypt, out of the house where they were slaves. I said:

L.13: "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel: I made a covenant with your fathers on the day I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slaves, saying,

R.13: "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says: When I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, where they lived as slaves, I made a covenant with them. I told them:

decisions.choice: I made a covenant: the LORD's covenant set beside theirs
decisions.reason: The pronoun "I" is stressed. Before the people made their covenant in the temple (verses 8, 15), the LORD had made his own with their ancestors, and the law of release was part of it.

decisions.choice: the house of slaves: Israel's slavery in Egypt
decisions.reason: The words come from the opening of the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:2; Deuteronomy 5:6). A people the LORD freed from slavery must not keep their own brothers in slavery, as Deuteronomy 15:15 says in the law of release: "remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt".

decisions.choice: on the day: at the time
decisions.reason: "On the day" means at the time of the exodus and Sinai, not one particular day.

decisions.choice: out of the house where they were slaves (B); where they lived as slaves (R)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:2. "Slave" stays because Israel's slavery in Egypt is the point.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD (L); The LORD says this (B); This is what the LORD says (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula in Jeremiah.

records.source: מִקֵּ֣ץ שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֡ים תְּֽשַׁלְּח֡וּ אִישׁ֩ אֶת־אָחִ֨יו הָעִבְרִ֜י אֲשֶֽׁר־יִמָּכֵ֣ר לְךָ֗ וַעֲבָֽדְךָ֙ שֵׁ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֔ים וְשִׁלַּחְתּ֥וֹ חָפְשִׁ֖י מֵֽעִמָּ֑ךְ וְלֹֽא־שָׁמְע֤וּ אֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ אֵלַ֔י וְלֹ֥א הִטּ֖וּ אֶת־אָזְנָֽם׃
records.gloss: From [the] end of seven years you will send away each his brother the Hebrew who is sold to you, and he will serve you six years, and you will send him away free from with you; but not listened your fathers to me, and not they inclined their ear.
pieces: 'At the close of every seven years, each of you must release any fellow Hebrew who has been sold to you as a slave. When that person has served you six years, you must send them away free.' But your ancestors did not listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} or pay attention.

L.14: 'At the end of seven years you shall send away, each one, his brother, the Hebrew who is sold to you; he shall serve you six years, and you shall send him away free from you.' But your fathers did not listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} or incline their ear.

R.14: 'Every seven years, each of you must free any fellow Hebrew who was sold to you as a slave. After that person has worked for you for six years, you must let them go free.' But your ancestors did not listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} or pay attention.

decisions.choice: the law of release from Deuteronomy 15:1, 12 and Exodus 21:2
decisions.reason: The words join the law of the year of release, "at the end of seven years" (Deuteronomy 15:1), with the law that a Hebrew sold to you shall serve six years and then go free (Deuteronomy 15:12; Exodus 21:2). The LORD quotes his own law in a shortened form.

decisions.choice: at the end of seven years: in the seventh year
decisions.reason: The phrase counts seven years and names the last of them, as in Deuteronomy 15:1. The next clause makes it plain: after six years of service the slave goes free.

decisions.choice: is sold: sold, or sells himself, because of debt
decisions.reason: As in Deuteronomy 15:12, the verb form can mean "is sold" or "sells himself". A Hebrew came into slavery through poverty or debt.

decisions.choice: incline their ear: pay attention
decisions.reason: To turn the ear toward someone is to listen with care. The same words are used of the ancestors in 7:24, 26 and 11:8.

decisions.choice: any fellow Hebrew ... that person ... them
decisions.reason: "His brother, the Hebrew" means a fellow Israelite, man or woman, as verse 9 and Deuteronomy 15:12 show. Balanced and Readable use words that include both, as Deuteronomy 15:12 does. "Slave" stays, as in verse 9.

decisions.choice: At the close of every seven years
decisions.reason: The same wording as Deuteronomy 15:1, which these words quote.

records.source: וַתָּשֻׁ֨בוּ אַתֶּ֜ם הַיּ֗וֹם וַתַּעֲשׂ֤וּ אֶת־הַיָּשָׁר֙ בְּעֵינַ֔י לִקְרֹ֥א דְר֖וֹר אִ֣ישׁ לְרֵעֵ֑הוּ וַתִּכְרְת֤וּ בְרִית֙ לְפָנַ֔י בַּבַּ֕יִת אֲשֶׁר־נִקְרָ֥א שְׁמִ֖י עָלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And turned you today, and you did the right in my eyes, to proclaim liberty each to his neighbor; and you made [a] covenant before me in the house which is called my name on it.
pieces: Just now you yourselves turned back and did what is right in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight: each of you announced freedom for your neighbor, and you made a covenant in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} presence in the house that bears {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.

L.15: And you turned today and did what is right in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes, by proclaiming liberty, each to his neighbor; and you made a covenant before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in the house that is called by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.

R.15: Just now you changed your ways and did what I say is right. Each of you announced freedom for your neighbor. You made a covenant in front of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, in the temple that bears {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.

decisions.choice: you turned today: you repented recently
decisions.reason: "Today" here means "just now", in these recent days. "Turned" is the word used for turning back to God, repenting; the next verse uses it again for turning away (verse 11 m2).

decisions.choice: his neighbor: a fellow Israelite held as a slave
decisions.reason: The slave is called the owner's "neighbor", a member of the same people, as "brother" in verses 9 and 14.

decisions.choice: the house called by my name: the temple
decisions.reason: The covenant was sworn in the temple, before the LORD, which made the oath all the more binding. The same phrase is used of the temple in 7:10-11.

decisions.choice: Just now
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "today" means here (m1).

decisions.choice: the temple
decisions.reason: Readable names the house as the temple (m3).

records.source: וַתָּשֻׁ֨בוּ֙ וַתְּחַלְּל֣וּ אֶת־שְׁמִ֔י וַתָּשִׁ֗בוּ אִ֤ישׁ אֶת־עַבְדּוֹ֙ וְאִ֣ישׁ אֶת־שִׁפְחָת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁר־שִׁלַּחְתֶּ֥ם חָפְשִׁ֖ים לְנַפְשָׁ֑ם וַתִּכְבְּשׁ֣וּ אֹתָ֔ם לִֽהְי֣וֹת לָכֶ֔ם לַעֲבָדִ֖ים וְלִשְׁפָחֽוֹת׃ס
records.gloss: But you turned and you profaned my name, and you brought back each his male slave and each his female slave whom you had sent away free to their desire, and you subjected them to be for you as male slaves and as female slaves.
pieces: But then you turned around and profaned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. Each of you took back the male and female slaves you had set free to go where they wished, and you forced them to be your slaves again.

L.16: But then you turned and profaned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and you brought back, each his male slave and each his female slave whom you had sent away free as they desired, and you subjected them to be male slaves and female slaves for you.

R.16: But then you turned around and dishonored {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. Each of you took back the slaves you had freed to live as they wanted. You forced them to be your slaves again.

decisions.choice: profaned my name: dishonored the LORD by breaking an oath sworn in his name
decisions.reason: The covenant was sworn before the LORD in his temple (verse 15). To break it was to treat his name as worthless, as Leviticus 19:12 warns: "You shall not swear falsely by my name, and so profane the name of your God."

decisions.choice: to their desire: free to go where they chose
decisions.reason: The phrase, literally "to their soul", means as they themselves wished, as in Deuteronomy 21:14. The freed slaves had been their own masters.

decisions.choice: subjected: brought under force
decisions.reason: The verb means to subdue or press down, used of conquering a land (Joshua 18:1) and of forcing people into slavery (Nehemiah 5:5).

decisions.choice: slave at every level
decisions.reason: As in verse 9: slavery itself is the point of the passage.

decisions.choice: dishonored
decisions.reason: Readable says "dishonored" for the less common word "profaned".

records.source: לָכֵן֮ כֹּה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֒ אַתֶּם֙ לֹֽא־שְׁמַעְתֶּ֣ם אֵלַ֔י לִקְרֹ֣א דְר֔וֹר אִ֥ישׁ לְאָחִ֖יו וְאִ֣ישׁ לְרֵעֵ֑הוּ הִנְנִ֣י קֹרֵא֩ לָכֶ֨ם דְּר֜וֹר נְאֻם־יְהוָ֗ה אֶל־הַחֶ֨רֶב֙ אֶל־הַדֶּ֣בֶר וְאֶל־הָרָעָ֔ב וְנָתַתִּ֤י אֶתְכֶם֙ לְזַעֲוָ֔ה לְכֹ֖ל מַמְלְכ֥וֹת הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh: You not listened to me to proclaim liberty each to his brother and each to his neighbor; look I [am] proclaiming to you liberty, declaration of Yahweh, to the sword, to the pestilence and to the famine; and I will make you for a horror to all [the] kingdoms of the earth.
pieces: Therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: You have not obeyed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} by announcing freedom, each of you for your fellow Hebrew and your neighbor. So now I am announcing freedom for you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: freedom to fall by the sword, the plague and the famine. I will make you a horror to every kingdom on earth.

L.17: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: You have not listened to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} by proclaiming liberty, each to his brother and each to his neighbor. Look, I am proclaiming liberty to you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to the sword, to the pestilence and to the famine; and I will make you a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.

R.17: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: You did not obey {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. You did not give freedom to your own people and your neighbors. So now I will give you freedom, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: freedom to die by war, disease and famine! I will make you something that horrifies every kingdom on earth.

decisions.choice: I am proclaiming liberty to you: the LORD answers their broken release with a release of his own
decisions.reason: The word for the release they took back is turned on them. Since they would not set their slaves free, the LORD sets them "free": he lets them go from his protection and gives them over to the sword, disease and famine. The punishment matches the sin in its very words.

decisions.choice: to the sword, to the pestilence, to the famine: handed over to them
decisions.reason: The word "to" says where their "freedom" takes them: they are released into the power of these three disasters.

decisions.choice: a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth: the curse of Deuteronomy 28:25
decisions.reason: As in 15:4; 24:9; 29:18, the covenant curse of Deuteronomy 28:25 comes true: what happens to them will make other nations shudder.

decisions.choice: horror: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: As in 15:4 and 24:9, the written Hebrew text spells this word with two letters in a different order, and the scribes noted the usual form in the margin to be read aloud. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: the sword, the pestilence, the famine (L); the sword, the plague, the famine (B); war, disease, famine (R)
decisions.reason: The three disasters keep the wording settled for Jeremiah, in the order this verse gives them.

decisions.choice: freedom to fall by (B); freedom to die by (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat "freedom" and say what being released "to the sword" means, so that the irony is clear (m1, m2). Literal keeps the bare "to".

decisions.choice: your fellow Hebrew (B); your own people (R)
decisions.reason: "His brother" means a fellow Israelite, as in verses 9 and 14.

records.source: וְנָתַתִּ֣י אֶת־הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים הָעֹֽבְרִים֙ אֶת־בְּרִתִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־הֵקִ֨ימוּ֙ אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֣י הַבְּרִ֔ית אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּרְת֖וּ לְפָנָ֑י הָעֵ֨גֶל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּרְת֣וּ לִשְׁנַ֔יִם וַיַּעַבְר֖וּ בֵּ֥ין בְּתָרָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And I will make the men, the [ones] transgressing my covenant, who not they carried out [the] words of the covenant which they cut before me, the calf which they cut in two and they passed between its parts,
pieces: As for {{gender:the people|the men}} who broke {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant and did not keep the terms of the covenant they made before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I will make them like the calf they cut in two and walked between its halves,

L.18: And I will make {{gender:the people|the men}} who transgressed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant, who did not carry out the words of the covenant that they made before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, [like] the calf that they cut in two and passed between its parts,

R.18: These people broke {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant. They did not keep the promises they made in front of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} when they cut a calf in two and walked between the halves. So I will make them like that calf.

decisions.choice: the calf cut in two: a rite of oath-taking
decisions.reason: Those who made the covenant cut a young bull in two, laid out the halves, and walked between them. By doing so they called down on themselves the fate of the animal if they broke their word: may it be done to me as to this calf. The same rite lies behind Genesis 15:9-17, where Abram lays out the halves of the animals and the LORD, as a smoking fire pot and a flaming torch, passes between the pieces to seal his covenant.

decisions.choice: I will make the people ... like the calf
alternatives: I will give the men ... (over to their enemies, verse 20); the calf names the covenant rite
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "I will give the men ... the calf", with no word for "like". The verse is taken as saying that the LORD will make them like the calf they cut: they will suffer the fate they called down on themselves (verse 20). Another reading joins "the calf" to the covenant ("the covenant they made before me, the calf that they cut"), but then "I will give the men" has no completion until verse 20.

decisions.choice: transgressed ... passed: one Hebrew verb; made ... cut: another
decisions.reason: The verb for "transgress" also means "pass over" or "pass through": those who passed between the halves of the calf have passed over the covenant. And the Hebrew for "making" a covenant is "cutting" one, the word used for cutting the calf. The rite and the sin are told in the same words.

decisions.choice: [like] (L); like (B)
decisions.reason: The word is supplied to make sense of the sentence (m2). Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: three sentences, with the judgment last
decisions.reason: Readable tells first what the people did and then what the LORD will do.

records.source: שָׂרֵ֨י יְהוּדָ֜ה וְשָׂרֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם הַסָּֽרִסִים֙ וְהַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים וְכֹ֖ל עַ֣ם הָאָ֑רֶץ הָעֹ֣בְרִ֔ים בֵּ֖ין בִּתְרֵ֥י הָעֵֽגֶל׃
records.gloss: [the] princes of Judah and [the] princes of Jerusalem, the eunuchs and the priests and all [the] people of the land, the [ones] passing between [the] parts of the calf;
pieces: that is, the officials of Judah and the officials of Jerusalem, the court officers, the priests and all the people of the land who walked between the halves of the calf.

L.19: the princes of Judah and the princes of Jerusalem, the eunuchs and the priests and all the people of the land, who passed between the parts of the calf;

R.19: These were the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem, the palace officials, the priests and all the people of the land. They had all walked between the halves of the calf.

decisions.choice: eunuchs: royal court officers, perhaps castrated men
decisions.reason: The word names a class of officers at the king's court. Many such officers in the courts of the ancient Near East were castrated, but the word is also used of high officials who were not, so here it may mean palace officials in general (compare 29:2; 38:7; 2 Kings 24:12).

decisions.choice: the people of the land: the free landowning citizens of Judah
decisions.reason: The phrase names the ordinary citizens of the land, as against the court and the priests, who often stood together on matters of state (2 Kings 11:14; 23:30). Every class of the nation took part in the oath.

decisions.choice: a list naming the people of verse 18
decisions.reason: The verse says who the covenant-breakers were. The sentence goes on in verse 20 with what the LORD will do to them.

decisions.choice: princes, eunuchs (L); officials, court officers (B); leaders, palace officials (R)
decisions.reason: Two words for the king's court stand side by side, as in 2 Kings 24:12. Balanced uses "officials" for the princes as usual and calls the eunuchs "court officers" to keep the groups apart; Readable has "leaders" and "palace officials".

decisions.choice: that is (B); These were (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add a few words to show that the list names the people of verse 18.

records.source: וְנָתַתִּ֤י אוֹתָם֙ בְּיַ֣ד אֹֽיְבֵיהֶ֔ם וּבְיַ֖ד מְבַקְשֵׁ֣י נַפְשָׁ֑ם וְהָיְתָ֤ה נִבְלָתָם֙ לְמַֽאֲכָ֔ל לְע֥וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וּלְבֶהֱמַ֥ת הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: and I will give them into [the] hand of their enemies and into [the] hand of [those] seeking their life; and will be their corpse for food for [the] birds of the heavens and for [the] beasts of the earth.
pieces: I will hand them over to their enemies, to those who want them dead, and their dead bodies will become food for the birds of the sky and for the wild animals.

L.20: and I will give them into the hand of their enemies and into the hand of those who seek their life; and their corpses will be food for the birds of the heavens and for the beasts of the earth.

R.20: I will hand them over to their enemies, who want to kill them. The birds and the wild animals will eat their dead bodies.

decisions.choice: those who seek their life: those who want to kill them
decisions.reason: As in 21:7 and 19:7, to seek someone's life is to try to kill them.

decisions.choice: food for the birds and the beasts: the covenant curse of Deuteronomy 28:26
decisions.reason: As in 7:33 and 19:7. Those who walked between the halves of the calf will lie like its carcass, food for birds of prey, as the birds came down on Abram's animals in Genesis 15:11.

decisions.choice: the birds of the sky and the wild animals (B); the birds and the wild animals (R)
decisions.reason: As in 7:33.

records.source: וְאֶת־צִדְקִיָּ֨הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֜ה וְאֶת־שָׂרָ֗יו אֶתֵּן֙ בְּיַ֣ד אֹֽיְבֵיהֶ֔ם וּבְיַ֖ד מְבַקְשֵׁ֣י נַפְשָׁ֑ם וּבְיַד חֵ֚יל מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל הָעֹלִ֖ים מֵעֲלֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And Zedekiah king of Judah and his princes I will give into [the] hand of their enemies and into [the] hand of [those] seeking their life, and into [the] hand of [the] army of [the] king of Babylon, the [ones] going up from on you.
pieces: Zedekiah king of Judah and his officials I will hand over to their enemies, to those who want them dead, to the army of the king of Babylon, which has withdrawn from you.

L.21: And Zedekiah king of Judah and his princes I will give into the hand of their enemies and into the hand of those who seek their life, and into the hand of the army of the king of Babylon, which has gone up from you.

R.21: I will hand over Zedekiah king of Judah and his leaders to their enemies, who want to kill them. I will hand them over to the army of the king of Babylon, which has gone away from you for now.

decisions.choice: gone up from you: broken off the siege
decisions.reason: An army that "goes up from" a city it is attacking marches away (21:2). The Babylonians had left Jerusalem for a time to meet an Egyptian army (37:5, 11).

decisions.choice: Zedekiah and his officials: what happened when the city fell
decisions.reason: The king and his officials were caught by the Babylonians when they fled from the city. Zedekiah was blinded and taken to Babylon, and the nobles of Judah were put to death (39:4-7; 52:7-11, 24-27).

decisions.choice: princes (L); officials (B); leaders (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 10.

decisions.choice: for now
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the withdrawal was only for a time, as verse 22 shows.

records.source: הִנְנִ֨י מְצַוֶּ֜ה נְאֻם־יְהוָ֗ה וַהֲשִׁ֨בֹתִ֜ים אֶל־הָעִ֤יר הַזֹּאת֙ וְנִלְחֲמ֣וּ עָלֶ֔יהָ וּלְכָד֖וּהָ וּשְׂרָפֻ֣הָ בָאֵ֑שׁ וְאֶת־עָרֵ֧י יְהוּדָ֛ה אֶתֵּ֥ן שְׁמָמָ֖ה מֵאֵ֥ין יֹשֵֽׁב׃פ
records.gloss: Look I [am] commanding, declaration of Yahweh, and I will bring them back to the city this, and they will fight against it and capture it and burn it with the fire; and [the] cities of Judah I will make [a] desolation, without inhabitant.
pieces: I am about to give the order, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will bring them back to this city, and they will attack it, take it and burn it down. I will turn the towns of Judah into a desolate waste where no one lives."

L.22: Look, I am commanding, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and I will bring them back to this city, and they will fight against it and capture it and burn it with fire; and I will make the cities of Judah a desolation without inhabitant."

R.22: I am going to give the command, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will lead the army back to this city. They will attack it, capture it and burn it to the ground. I will make the towns of Judah an empty ruin where no one lives."

decisions.choice: I am commanding: the LORD directs the Babylonian army
decisions.reason: The army that withdrew comes back at the LORD's order. The relief that led the owners to take back their slaves will not last: the LORD himself will bring the enemy back (37:8).

decisions.choice: bring them back: the same verb as "took back" in verses 11 and 16
decisions.reason: The owners "brought back" their slaves; now the LORD will "bring back" the Babylonian army. The word that told their sin tells their punishment.

decisions.choice: the city captured and burned, the towns left empty
decisions.reason: Jerusalem fell in 586 BC and was burned (39:1-8; 52:12-14), and the towns of Judah were left in ruins.

decisions.choice: a desolate waste where no one lives (B); an empty ruin where no one lives (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "without inhabitant" as a clause, and Readable names the army for "them".
